summary.title: Speaking for Hackers
summary.one_liner: A free online guide by Ben Orenstein on preparing and delivering technical talks to programmer audiences, covering topic choice, proposals, slides, practice, and handling nerves and questions.
keywords: how to write a talk proposal
things not to say in a talk
takeaways: How to pick a talk topic and write a proposal that gets accepted
Structure tips such as cutting a long introduction and preparing for doubt
Practice, slide, and pre-talk checklist advice
Techniques for holding attention, handling questions, body language, and nerves during a talk
How to handle Q&A after the talk and save social proof
summary.summary: This is a multi-chapter online book, Version 1.0, by Ben Orenstein, aimed at helping programmers give talks that keep a room engaged. The page shows only the table of contents, split into before, during, and after the talk sections. Topics include choosing and proposing a talk, practicing, slide design, a pre-talk checklist, and managing doubt. Delivery chapters cover attention, questions, body language, stage movement, nervousness, and phrases to avoid. The visible text does not include the chapter bodies, so the specific advice is not confirmed here.
